citations.title: Should a football club build its own AI platform?
excerpts: # Build or buy? Inside a football operating system.
AI makes software easier to start. Football makes it hard to finish.
Jonathan Hazut, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer

The January transfer window changes squads, and the data has to keep up. A transfer can change a player’s league, provider identifiers and available coverage, and the system must not mistake a change in what can be observed for a change in the player.

Suppliers move too. Providers update their glossaries, new metrics arrive every month, and a club may switch providers overnight because the next annual fee no longer suits it. Each change reaches field meanings, identity matching and every analysis that uses them.

Marquee’s data-agnostic foundation absorbs these changes across the product. Our multi-tenant architecture keeps each club’s data and sporting DNA separate on a shared engineering foundation, and Kubernetes-managed deployments preserve every club’s configuration as models and software change.
For an internal build, this is the part that rarely appears in the original plan. It lasts as long as the system does.

citations.title: Half a Pattern: how Marquee reads what a squad is short of
excerpts: # Half a Pattern: is a squad’s weakest position the right place to sign?

The hardest part of recruitment is knowing what to look for. Coherent sides produce certain qualities together, and many squads deliver one half of a pairing and not the other. That gap is often somewhere other than the weakest position.
Tal Darchi, Co-founder and Chief Data Scientist

Across a worldwide pool of team seasons, certain qualities tend to rise and fall together. Sides that create good chances also put shots on target. Teams that keep the ball tend to move it into the final third. Those patterns form a standard, and the first read asks where this squad delivers one half of a pairing but not the other.

The second read is the team’s own game. The standard says what coherent sides do in general. A team’s style says which of those pairings it actually plays through. Together they leave a ranked list of relevant pairings where one side falls short of what the other implies, with the clearest at the top.

Only then do we look at players. Each pairing that falls short points to a position and to the squad’s own players on each side of it, by name, which determines what each candidate is measured on. His level on that quality is a percentile against players in the same position in our data pool, with the search scoped to leagues around the club’s own level. We also ask whether he carries the qualities that usually travel with the missing one, because one half of a pattern is more useful with the rest of it. Where the match data allows, the read also checks whether a pairing happens on the pitch: whose passes reach whose runs, and which connections go unused.
Four-step sequence: the worldwide standard, the team’s own game, position and names, the ranking.
The measurement is positional. The question comes from the squad. Choosing that question is most of the work.

Stronger teams do more of everything. Compare teams side by side and every attacking number seems linked to every other, because good teams rack them all up. We tested for this effect and take it into account, so the pairings reflect how sides are built rather than how good they are.

citations.title: Marquee partners with Club Atlético Lanús
excerpts: # Marquee becomes the official intelligence layer of Club Atlético Lanús

Marquee is now the official intelligence layer of [Club Atlético Lanús](https://www.linkedin.com/company/clublanus/) . The reigning Copa Sudamericana and Recopa Sudamericana champions, and among Argentina’s most respected developers of talent, are enhancing their scouting and analysis with Marquee, turning their external and internal data into answers shaped by Lanús’s own way of seeing the game, across recruitment, analysis, squad management and opponent preparation.

“Our job is to find the right players before anyone else does. Marquee lets us cover more ground in less time and bring modern tools into how we operate, without losing the judgement that has always defined this club,” said [Matías Sarue](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matias-sarue/en/) , Chief Scout at Club Atlético Lanús.

“Lanús win by seeing the game more clearly than clubs with far bigger budgets. That is exactly the kind of club we built Marquee for,” said Dean Bracha, Co-Founder and CEO of Marquee. “Working with Matías and his team, our job is to give that judgement more room to do what it does best.”

citations.title: Senior AI Scientist - Marquee - Herzlia | DevJobs
excerpts: Marquee builds AI that helps professional football clubs make better decisions about recruitment, squad planning and match preparation. We combine football data, machine learning and generative AI to turn complex analysis into practical insights for coaches, analysts and recruitment teams.

We are looking for a Senior AI Scientist to develop the models behind our football intelligence platform. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of research projects from problem definition and experimentation through production and ongoing evaluation. You will work closely with our data, engineering, product and football experts on questions such as how a player may perform in a new league, how well they fit a team's playing style, and how teams can prepare for different opponents.
* Lead applied AI research for player evaluation, performance forecasting, tactical fit and team analysis.
* Turn open football questions into testable hypotheses and clear modelling objectives.
* Design, train and improve models using match events, player and team histories, and spatial or tracking data where available.
* Build rigorous evaluations with credible baselines, tests on later seasons and unseen competitions, and explicit checks for data leakage, uncertainty and failure cases.
* Partner with engineers to bring models into production, monitor their performance and improve reliability, latency and inference cost.
* Collaborate on LLM and agent workflows that retrieve verified data and use model outputs to produce traceable football analysis.
* Help shape research priorities, review code and experiments, and share methods and findings with the team.

* 5+ years of relevant experience in machine learning, AI research or data science, or equivalent depth through substantial applied research, with evidence of independently delivering complex projects.
* Strong Python skills and practical experience with PyTorch, SQL and scientific computing tools such as pandas and NumPy.
* Solid foundations in machine learning, deep learning, statistics and experimental design, with the judgement to select methods that fit the problem.
* Experience building and evaluating predictive models using large, imperfect datasets, including an understanding of missing data, selection bias and changing data distributions.
* Strong background in data structures, algorithms, and machine learning fundamentals, with a deep understanding of data science methodologies and best practices.
* Experience working with complex, high-dimensional football and sports datasets, including event data, tracking data, and physical/biometric metrics.
* Proficiency in building automated data pipelines, ETL processes, and validation checks for heterogeneous external and internal data sources.
* A track record of turning research into working products, with reproducible experiments, maintainable code and collaboration with engineering teams.
* The ability to explain technical findings and limitations clearly, work independently and learn from product colleagues and domain experts.
* An MSc or PhD in computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering or a related field.
* Experience with transformers, sequence modelling, representation learning or self-supervised learning.
* Experience building and evaluating LLM applications, retrieval systems or tool-using agents.
* Experience with ranking and recommendation systems, probabilistic modelling or causal inference.
* Experience with sports analytics, event or tracking data, or a strong interest in football.

You will own research that reaches professional football clubs and work closely with the people who use it. The role offers room to explore new methods, influence the product and judge success by whether your models help clubs make better decisions.

Show us research that reached real use. Please include your CV and a short example of an AI project you took from research to practical use, explaining the problem, your contribution and how you evaluated the result.

basis.reasoning: The complete readable Senior AI Scientist job posting describes AI research, data science and product work but names no CRM or sales/marketing system, so the list is empty.

Inside Marquee, clubs can put their SkillCorner Physical and Game Intelligence metrics to work across every Player 360 scout report, Discovery query and opponent analysis, each shaped by their club’s sporting DNA and drawing on everything else the platform unifies.
“SkillCorner’s reputation speaks for itself. We’re here to empower our clients to make the best of their Physical and Game Intelligence data,” said Dean Bracha, Co-Founder and CEO of Marquee.
Both companies are building for the same clubs and the same goal: better football decisions, reached faster.
